Closes #19869 (tickless support issue)

issue_context.title: xilinx_zynqmp: k_busy_wait() never returns if called with interrupts locked
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
k_busy_wait() never returns if called with interrupts locked on the `qemu_cortex_r5` platform, which uses the `xilinx_zynqmp` SoC with `xlnx_psttc_timer` system timer.

For more details, refer to the issue #23519.

**Proposed solution**
Switch the timer mode of operation from "Interval" to "Match" (i.e. convert it to a "running timer") and return its register value.

review_comments: Dumb question: is there a link to a public reference for this hardware?  This would be a good place to put that if you have it.

The Xilinx TTC (well, it is a Cadence IP core that has been customised by Xilinx) is used on the Xilinx ZynqMP (now called UltraScale+) SoC.

"Zynq UltraScale+ Device Technical Reference Manual" provides documentation for the TTC.
Ditto, though I guess DTS constants are really ugly, so I feel less strongly about this one.
yes, they get very long and ugly soon after this.
Style: unless this is needed to keep line lengths under control, I'd prefer to see the existing kconfig used directly instead of a local synonym.

Would be good to have a comment explaining how this value was chosen.  There's a lot of value in making these "minimum time to next tick" clamps as low as possible, and tuning them has been subtle and difficult in the past.  If this is a conservative WAG, that's fine, but we should say so.
This was a conservative value set using the "trial and error" approach. I will add an in-line comment about this mentioning that there is a room for improvement/further optimisation here.
Style: "IRQ_CONNECT(TIMER_IRQ, ..." sufficiently implies that the timer interrupt is connected without the comment. :)

Just wanted to provide a logical flow of this function in the comments (i.e. even without reading actual code, you will know what this function does just only reading comments).

Though, I agree that this would often qualify as a "state-the-obvious" kind of comment :p
